h1: Dener vertical machining centers — TMC VMCs and TDC double-column, BBT40 and BBT50
intro: A machining centre mills, drills, bores and taps prismatic parts under CNC and changes its own tools from a magazine, so a part that once went from the mill to the drill press to the tapping arm is finished in one setup. NovoTech sells Dener's machining centres in Canada, built in Kayseri, Turkey: the TMC vertical machining centres (VMC) in five sizes, from the TMC 850 with 33.5 × 20.1 × 22″ (850 × 510 × 560 mm) travels to the TMC 1600 with 63 × 27.6 × 27.6″ (1,600 × 700 × 700 mm), all with a direct-drive BBT40 spindle at 10,000 rpm, a 24-tool arm changer and rapids of 1,417 in/min (36 m/min); and the TDC double-column (gantry) machining centres for long, wide and heavy parts — 82.7 to 161.4″ (2,100 – 4,100 mm) of X travel, 55 to 82.7″ between the columns, tables to 157.5 × 70.9″ for 26,455 lb (12,000 kg) and a BBT50 spindle with through-spindle coolant. Mitsubishi M80A control with Navi-Mill conversational programming as standard, Fanuc to order. Installed and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.a: A vertical machining centre carries the part on a table that moves in X and Y under a spindle on a single column — the standard machine for brackets, housings, plates and moulds up to the size of its table — 39 × 20″ to 69 × 28″ on the TMC. A double-column machine puts the spindle on a cross rail between two columns over a long table: it takes parts far wider and heavier than a vertical's single column could, keeps its rigidity over the whole width, and machines machine bases, plates, frames and large moulds. The TMC runs to 63 × 27.6″ of travel and 2,646 lb on the table; the TDC starts at 82.7 × 48″ and carries up to 26,455 lb.

faq.q: BBT40, BBT50 — will my CAT40 holders fit?
faq.a: BBT is BT with the BIG-PLUS dual-contact face: the holder seats on the taper and on the spindle face at once, which stiffens the tool. Standard BT holders fit a BBT spindle too. CAT40 holders do not: the taper is the same 7/24 but the flange and the pull stud are different, so plan for BT or BBT holders — we quote a starter set with the machine. BBT50 carries larger face mills and boring bars and takes heavier cuts than BBT40.

Dener specifies ±0.004 mm (±0.00016″) positioning and ±0.002 mm repeatability per 300 mm on the TMC (±0.005 mm on the TMC 1600), and ±0.008 / ±0.004 mm on the TDC. Double-nut C3 ballscrews coupled directly to the servo motors, roller linear guides, spindle cooling and stress-relieved Meehanite castings keep it there; linear scales are an option for closed-loop positioning.

faq.q: Which control, and how are they programmed?
faq.a: The Mitsubishi M80A with a 15″ touchscreen is standard, with Navi-Mill conversational programming for simple parts at the machine; Fanuc 0i-MF is an option. Both run ISO G-code from any CAM system, with rigid tapping, canned cycles and 4th-axis control for the optional rotary table.

Through-spindle coolant at 435 psi (30 bar) for deep drilling and pocketing (standard on the TDC); a 12,000 or 15,000 rpm spindle if you cut mostly aluminum; a tool setter and workpiece probe to cut setup time; a CNC rotary table for four-sided work; and linear scales for the tightest work. The chip conveyor, chip wash-down, oil skimmer and spindle cooling are standard.

faq.q: What foundation, power and air do they need?
faq.a: The TMC machines need 32 kVA (43 kVA for the 1300 and 1600), 73 – 87 psi of shop air and a level reinforced-concrete floor; the TDC machines, at 21 to 40 tonnes, sit on a foundation built to Dener's drawing. We send the drawings and the floor-space plan with the quote.

faq.q: Do you deliver, install and train in Canada?
faq.a: Yes. Machines ship from Kayseri to Mississauga, ON, Canada; NovoTech unloads, levels and commissions the machine, checks the geometry, trains your operators and programmers on the control and helps with the first parts. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, a 1-year warranty and parts and service from Mississauga. Ask for the foundation drawing and the power and air requirements before the machine ships.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
